Dogs naturally understand other dogs better than they understand us. The goal wasn't to make Ryder love every dog she sees-it was to teach her that she doesn't need to react to every dog she sees. Before training, a simple neighborhood walk was nearly impossible. Seeing another dog meant lunging, pulling, and trying to start conflict. Through obedience work and carefully controlled sessions with Bishop, Ryder learned a valuable lesson: not every dog is a threat, and not every situation requires a reaction. Also notice how Bishop's corrections increase in intensity throughout the video. He starts with the minimum amount of pressure necessary and only escalates when Ryder chooses not to listen. That's how dogs naturally communicate with one another. Will I tell these owners to take her to a dog park and expect her to be everyone's best friend? Absolutely not. But can we give her a better quality of life by helping her calmly walk past another dog across the street? Absolutely. Not every dog needs this type of training, but some dogs can benefit tremendously from it. idea from@Hax.aep. Football is one of the most popular sports in the world, and millions of people of all ages and genders enjoy watching and playing it. However, there are still stereotypes suggesting that girls know less about football than boys. While some girls may not be interested in the sport, many others are passionate supporters who understand tactics, players, clubs, and the history of the game just as well as any male fan. This discussion became more popular after Portuguese footballer Rafael Leão shared a controversial message on social media. He wrote: "Girls, the World Cup is over. Now you can stop pretending you understand football." The post quickly spread online and received a lot of criticism. Many people considered the comment sexist because it implied that female fans only pretend to understand football during major tournaments. After the backlash, Leão deleted the post and later said that people should not take his Instagram posts too seriously, suggesting that it was meant as a joke rather than a serious statement. The incident started a wider conversation about stereotypes in football. Many female fans pointed out that they have supported their clubs for years, watch matches every week, and have extensive knowledge of the sport. Others admitted that they only watch major tournaments like the World Cup, but they argued that this is also true for many men. Casual fans exist in every sport, regardless of gender. Football should be a sport that welcomes everyone. Some people know every detail about formations, tactics, and player statistics, while others simply enjoy watching exciting matches with friends and family. There is nothing wrong with being a new fan or learning more about the game over time. Every supporter starts somewhere. In conclusion, Rafael Leão's comment created a major debate because many people felt it reinforced an unfair stereotype about women and football. Whether it was intended as a joke or not, it reminded people that football is for everyone. Knowledge of the sport depends on personal interest and experience, not on whether someone is male or female. |#rafa #leao #womens #footy #theory
